title: Studio validations panel: the state machine "Next states" box eats a typed comma, so a second target cannot be typed in
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-alice · session_011y7As6kDA9BVrMsBR9rmrJ

Filing gate ① · Source: fleet · found by the #36567 dev (os-dev-report comment 7103741576 on #36567), outside that card's surface; L1-b's review of PR #36719 (record 7104299620) made no ruling on it. Pre-existing on main.

## What happens
`TransitionsField` in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectValidationsPanel.tsx` is a controlled text box whose value is re-rendered from the parsed target list on every keystroke. Typing `done,` parses to `['done']` and the box shows `done` again, so the comma is eaten; typing ` c` next gives `donec`. An admin typing a state machine row's next states key by key cannot get a second target in; only a paste, or typing between two existing names, works. Same parse expression on main 9348f02b and on the #36719 head.

## Done when
- Typing `done, closed` key by key in a row's "Next states" box yields the targets `['done', 'closed']` (the box keeps its own text while it is being edited and parses on change or blur).
- A pin types the string one key at a time and asserts the written targets; one ablation.

reach: Studio form (a state_machine validation row's "Next states" box), measured in a test render (RTL `fireEvent.change` per key: `done,` read back as `done`; then ` ` and `c` read back as `donec`); not yet in a browser.
Business reason: an admin defining a state machine in Studio cannot type a state with two allowed next states, which is the ordinary case, and gets a wrong single target with no error.
Reader: the o7-studio area of seat repo:objectstack#7 (Studio validations panel).
Dedupe: `TransitionsField` → 2 (#36567 open, the parent; #26731 closed); `"Next states" comma` → 7, the open ones #36567 (parent) and #6015 (a seat post, unrelated); `ObjectValidationsPanel comma` → 3 (#36567 open; #2657, #27377 closed).
Suggested-grade: p2 · area:build · Bug · builders, often (every multi-target row typed in Studio) · measured in a test render.
